concepts.title: Basis and History of International Trade
concepts.definition: International trade is the exchange of goods and services across national boundaries, based on differences in resource endowments, technology and specialisation; historically it moved from the Silk Route and medieval spice trade to the slave trade and the industrial-era exchange of raw materials for manufactures.
concepts.key_idea: Trade follows comparative advantage: nations export what their resources and skills produce best and import the rest.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy108.txt trade basis, Silk Route, slave trade and industrial trade history
question_patterns: define international trade and its basis
trace the Silk Route's role in early trade
how did the slave trade shape Atlantic commerce
what changed with the industrial revolution in trade patterns
distinguish bilateral and multilateral trade
give examples of resource-based and skill-based exports

solution_steps.explain: unequal endowments and specialisation make exchange beneficial
the Silk Route carried silk and ideas; the triangular trade moved slaves and cotton
factories turned colonies into raw material suppliers and captive markets

concepts.title: Balance of Trade
concepts.definition: Balance of trade is the difference between the value of a country's exports and its imports in a year; exports exceeding imports give a positive or favourable balance, imports exceeding exports a negative or unfavourable balance.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting import value from export value yields the trade balance, positive when exports lead.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy108.txt balance of trade definition (positive and negative)
question_patterns: define balance of trade with its formula
compute a trade balance from export and import values
when is the balance called favourable
why is an unfavourable balance a concern
how does trade balance link to foreign exchange
give an example of a country with a favourable balance

solution_steps.explain: exports and imports are valued in a common currency
a positive result is a favourable balance

concepts.title: World Trade Patterns and Institutions
concepts.section: World Trade Organisation and Trade Blocs
concepts.definition: World trade is dominated by developed regions which exchange manufactures and services, while developing countries export primary products and low-skill manufactures; the World Trade Organisation regulates multilateral trade rules, and regional blocs like the EU and NAFTA liberalise trade within groups.
concepts.key_idea: The terms of trade debate centres on falling primary product prices against rising manufactured goods prices, keeping developing exporters disadvantaged.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy108.txt world trade patterns, WTO and trade blocs sections
question_patterns: describe the pattern of world trade between regions
what does the World Trade Organisation do
name major trade blocs and their purpose
why do developing countries seek fairer terms of trade
contrast exports of developed and developing countries
how do trade blocs both help and hinder global trade

solution_steps.explain: developed regions sell manufactures and services; developing regions sell primaries
the WTO frames and enforces multilateral trade rules
the EU and NAFTA internalise free trade while protecting their borders

concepts.title: Ports as Gateways of Trade
concepts.definition: Ports are the gateways of international trade, classified as commercial, oil, fishing, container and refuge ports; gateway ports like London and Singapore command hinterlands and forelands, linking the interior with overseas markets.
concepts.key_idea: A port's power lies in its hinterland's produce and its foreland's connections, which is why container hubs dominate modern shipping.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy108.txt port types, hinterland and foreland discussion
question_patterns: define ports and their major types
explain hinterland and foreland of a port
what makes a port a gateway port
why have container ports grown in importance
name two great gateway ports of the world
relate port efficiency to trade competitiveness

solution_steps.explain: commercial, oil, fishing, container and refuge ports serve distinct trades
hinterland is the producing interior; foreland is the overseas market side
standardised boxes and gantry cranes cut turnaround time, crowning hub ports

worked_examples.question_pattern: A country exports goods worth 800 billion currency units and imports worth 950 billion. Compute its trade balance and state its nature.
Explain hinterland and foreland using a major port.

solution_template.explain: the port's interior supplies exports and absorbs imports along rail-road links
the overseas shipping destinations form the market side of the port
Singapore thrives because both its lands are vast and well linked

worked_examples.question_pattern: State two functions of the WTO and one criticism of it by developing countries.

solution_template.explain: the WTO frames multilateral rules for goods, services and intellectual property
it settles trade disputes among member states
developing countries argue that farm subsidies of rich states skew the terms of trade
